exercise.title: Why are velocity and acceleration derivatives of position?

statement.p: If s(t) is position, then v=s' and a=v'=s''. In your own words, why do those two derivatives deserve the names velocity and acceleration, and why is \dfrac{d^2s}{dt^2} not the square of \dfrac{ds}{dt}?

hint.p: Velocity is the rate of change of position. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity. The superscript 2 counts how many times we differentiate.

exercise.title: Why can velocity be zero while acceleration is not?

statement.p: At the highest point of a throw, velocity is 0 but acceleration is still the gravitational constant. In your own words, why does that not contradict the meaning of a derivative, and why is it a mistake to say gravity turns off at the top?

hint.p: A value of a function can be zero while the function is still changing. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, not the velocity itself.

subsection.title: Units and signs in motion problems
subsection.p: The hardest part of many motion problems is not differentiating. It is deciding what the signs mean.
A position is measured relative to an origin. A velocity is measured relative to a positive direction. Acceleration tells whether velocity is increasing or decreasing in that chosen direction.
Acceleration does not directly tell which way the object is moving. Velocity does that.
Acceleration tells how velocity is changing.

paragraphs.title: Speeding up and slowing down
paragraphs.p: an object speeds up when the magnitude of velocity increases.

p.me: \text{if \(v\) and \(a\) have the same sign, the object is speeding up,}
\text{if \(v\) and \(a\) have opposite signs, the object is slowing down.}

paragraphs.p: The signs are opposite, so the ball is slowing down as it rises.
The signs are the same, so the ball is speeding up as it falls.

paragraphs.title: Same physical motion, different sign convention
paragraphs.p: Suppose a stone is dropped from a 100-meter tower.
If height above the ground is the position, and upward is positive, then
Both velocity and acceleration are negative after the stone is released, so the stone is speeding up downward.
If instead we measure downward distance from the release point, then the same motion is described by
Now velocity and acceleration are positive because the positive direction has been chosen downward.
The physics did not change. The coordinate choice changed.

exercise.title: Why must origin and positive direction be chosen before signs mean anything?

statement.p: The same falling stone can have negative or positive acceleration depending on whether upward or downward is called positive. In your own words, why does that not change the physics, and how do the signs of v and a together tell whether the object is speeding up?

hint.p: Signs are relative to a chosen axis. Speed increases when velocity and acceleration point the same way along that axis.
